science.qualification: Photosphere color of a Planck spectrum at the published temperature, 3,650 K, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 computes from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 3,650 K (the record) and log g 4.03 (from the record's mass and radius (packages/astronomy/data/bodies/roxs-42b.json)): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 91
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 19.9 hours, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 91 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 13%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 4.4%, the light's own noise being 0.63%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 0.83 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.69, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 29 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 8.9% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 91

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffcb93, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 91 (April and May 2025): the map's scale, 92% to 108% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 13% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · April and May 2025
